description: The highest-leverage review point in the context-engineering methodology is the one chief lacks entirely: RESEARCH. 'Misunderstandings can generate thousands of bad lines' — a wrong mental model of the codebase is the most expensive error an agent can make, and it is made before a single line is written. Chief's agent starts each story cold with the tasklist's acceptance criteria and whatever it greps in-iteration, which means every story in a tasklist independently re-derives (and can independently mis-derive) the same understanding of the code. This tasklist adds a RESEARCH PHASE that runs ONCE per tasklist, before the first story: sub-agents map the relevant code and return a STRUCTURED research document (target files, data flow, root cause, existing conventions), the document is reviewable by a human, and it is then carried into every story's context. Two independent benefits: correctness (the model works from a validated map instead of a fresh guess each time) and context economy (the research document is a compaction artifact — the methodology's core technique — so per-story iterations spend their window on the change rather than on rediscovery, holding the recommended 40-60% utilization). Talos already proves the shape: its Test Director derives expectation specs FROM THE DIFF and never lets the implementing agent author its own oracle — the same separation applies here. Sub-agents must return structured summaries, never raw grep output ('getting subagents to return structured output is not trivial'). Scope: `engine/driver.sh` (a per-tasklist pre-phase), `engine/agent.sh` (research dispatch + context injection), `docs/`. See ../AGENTIC-ENGINEERING-ADVISORY.md §2.2 and §6.2.

userStories.title: A once-per-tasklist research phase producing a structured document
userStories.description: Before the first story, run research and persist a structured artifact. Not prose — a map.
acceptanceCriteria: A research phase runs ONCE per tasklist before the first story and emits a structured research document with documented required sections: target files and why each is relevant, the data/control flow through them, the root-cause hypothesis or the change's point of insertion, and the existing conventions the implementation must follow

Research is delegated to sub-agent context(s) whose output is a STRUCTURED SUMMARY, not raw tool output — the parent's window receives the map, never the greps and file dumps that produced it (sub-agent context isolation)
The document is persisted under `.chief/state/` per tasklist, survives process death, and is REUSED on resume rather than regenerated — a resumed tasklist must not pay for research twice
The phase is bounded (a documented iteration/time budget) and its failure is a distinct, actionable state, never a silent fall-through into implementation

userStories.title: Carry the research into every story, and let a human correct it
userStories.description: The artifact is only worth its cost if stories consume it and a human can fix it when it is wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: Each story's iteration receives the research document in context (alongside the existing `progress.txt` and prior notes), so a story starts from the validated map instead of rediscovering it — and the mechanism is documented in `.chief/agent-context.md`/`templates/agent-context.md`

The research document is a reviewable artifact: it is written to a predictable path a human can read and EDIT between iterations, and an edited document is what subsequent stories consume (correcting research must be cheaper than correcting code — that is the entire point of the leverage hierarchy)

When the plan-review checkpoint (`89`) is enabled for the same tasklist, research is reviewable on the same surface and in the same order (research before plan); the two features compose without either becoming a hard dependency of the other
Research is opt-in or defaulted per a documented rule (the methodology says ~40% of tasks are one-shots that should skip it) — a small doc-fix tasklist must not pay a research iteration
userStories.notes: Injected via _compose_prompt so implement AND plan turns share one map; _research_refresh re-seeds it from the durable store at the top of every iteration, so a human edit between stories is what the next story reads. research_review_gate reviews the map on plannotator before any plan turn, reusing review.sh's primitives and returning 0 unless the tasklist already set review:plan — neither feature depends on the other. Opt-in rule written into templates/.chief agent-context.md, docs/reference/tasklist-schema.md and engine/instructions.md. Verified: .chief/verify.sh green end to end — quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 455->465, tol 15), VERSION-BUMP PASS (0.8.37), DOC-SYNC PASS, all 27 hermetic behavioral tests pass under the bystander guard, test/plan-review.sh PASS re-run directly. Gate paths exercised against a fake reviewer: review off -> rc 0; no review.sh -> rc 2; non-interactive -> rc 2 with no verdict written; annotated -> rc 1 + doc dropped + feedback captured; approved -> rc 0; re-asked never (already-approved short-circuit); a mutated map DOES re-ask (checksum binding); rounds budget parks at 3/3.

userStories.title: Document the contract and pin it with a hermetic test
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/` documents the research phase: the required sections, the sub-agent structured-output contract, the persistence path, the reuse-on-resume guarantee, the human-edit path, and the when-to-skip rule

A hermetic test asserts: the research document is produced once and carries the required sections; a second story in the same tasklist consumes it WITHOUT re-running research; a resumed run reuses the persisted document; a hand-edited document is the version subsequent stories receive
userStories.notes: docs/research-phase.md (linked from docs/README.md — "a document not linked here does not exist" — plus plan-review.md, tasklist-schema.md and the agent-context template) covers the four required sections, the sub-agent structured-output contract, the durable path .chief/state/research/<name>.md, the reuse-on-resume guarantee, the hand-edit surface, the when-to-skip rule and the exit-6 RESEARCH-FAILED state. test/research.sh pins all four assertions the criterion names. Observed: .chief/verify.sh green end to end — doc-link ratchet 4 dead vs 4 on main (no regression), quality ratchet OK (function_length_max 455->465 tol 15, single_use_functions 34->31, duplicate_blocks 0->0), bash -n clean on every shell file, VERSION-BUMP PASS (0.8.38), DOC-SYNC PASS, and all 28 hermetic behavioral tests green under the bystander guard — [9/28] test/research.sh RESEARCH PASS, with smoke, ratelimit, noworkguard, pause and teardown all passing in the same block. shellcheck is not installed on this host (the gate says so and skips; CI enforces it).
